question: Find the vector equation of the line passing through $A(-1,2,1)$ and $B(2,-2,4)$. Hence, obtain its Cartesian equation.
explanation:
Step 1: Position vector of the given point
The position vector of $A(-1,2,1)$ is
$$\vec{a}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}.$$
Step 2: Direction vector from the two points
The direction vector from $A$ to $B$ is
$$\overrightarrow{AB}=(2+1)\hat{i}+(-2-2)\hat{j}+(4-1)\hat{k}=3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}.$$
Step 3: Vector equation
Hence, the vector equation is
$$\vec{r}=-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}+\lambda(3\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}).$$
Step 4: Coordinate relations
Comparing components,
$$x=-1+3\lambda,\quad y=2-4\lambda,\quad z=1+3\lambda.$$
Step 5: Cartesian equation
Eliminating $\lambda$, we get
$$\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y-2}{-4}=\frac{z-1}{3}.$$
Thus, these are respectively the required vector and Cartesian equations of the line.

options.A: $\vec r=(-\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i-4\hat j+3\hat k)$; $\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y-2}{-4}=\frac{z-1}{3}$
options.B: $\vec r=(-\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i+4\hat j+3\hat k)$; $\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y-2}{4}=\frac{z-1}{3}$
options.C: $\vec r=(\hat i-2\hat j+\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i-4\hat j+3\hat k)$; $\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+2}{-4}=\frac{z-1}{3}$
options.D: $\vec r=(-\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i-4\hat j-3\hat k)$; $\frac{x+1}{3}=\frac{y-2}{-4}=\frac{z+1}{-3}$
